chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A one-eyed man blinded the eye of a healthy man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His eye is blinded.' I said: 'He remains blind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The right belongs to the one who was blinded.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for retaliating against a one-eyed person who blinds a healthy person?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'full equivalence' (kamal al-qisas) in eye injuries, establishing that the victim retains the right to choose between retaliation or blood money (diya). The Imam’s statement 'the truth is that he remains blind' underscores that the legal status of the victim does not change from 'one-eyed' to 'blind' merely by the loss of the second eye, preserving the option for full retaliation. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the victim's autonomy in selecting the appropriate form of retribution or compensation.
